annotation.title_clean: Guidance on privacy and developing and training generative AI models
annotation.title_en: Guidance on privacy and developing and training generative AI models
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)
annotation.summary_en: Australian privacy regulator guidance explaining how the Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles apply to developing and training generative AI models. It covers privacy by design, accuracy, data scraping, third-party datasets, sensitive information, secondary use, consent and notice. It has no robotics content.
key_provisions_or_claims: Publicly available data is not automatically usable for training generative AI; personal information obligations still apply.
Sensitive information, including many images, generally requires consent to collect; otherwise it must be deleted.
Secondary use of held data for AI training needs consent, or reasonable expectations plus a related purpose; opt-out is recommended.
Developers should take reasonable steps to ensure accuracy (APP 10) and use disclaimers.
Developers should adopt privacy by design and conduct privacy impact assessments.
